raw_segments.text: The undeveloped state of the class struggle, as well as their own surroundings, causes
socialists of this kind to consider themselves far superior to all class antagonisms.
They want to improve the condition of every member of society, even that of the most favored.
Hence, they habitually appeal to society at large, without distinction of class—nay,
by preference, to the ruling class.
For how can people, when once they understand their system, fail to see in it the best
possible plan of the best possible state of society?
